review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. All members of the IFRC workforce must contribute individually and collectively towards a working environment where everyone feels safe and empowered to perform their duties. The IFRC Country Cluster Delegation, based in Kinshasa, DRC, is the IFRC Secretariat’s frontline presence supporting Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, the Republic of the Congo, and Rwanda. It works to strengthen locally led, community‑based humanitarian action as the foundation of effective, sustainable response. Across the four countries, the Delegation supports a vast community‑based network of more than 1.2 million volunteers, over 600 staff, and more than 3,400 local units and 113 branches, ensuring deep territorial reach, including in hard‑to‑reach and high‑risk contexts. The Deputy Head of Delegation (DHoD) ensures continuity of leadership by managing specific areas of support that are ordinarily under the HoD’s remit and also deputises for the HoD when specifically delegated This role does not replace existing leadership profiles but complements them by ensuring that the delegation’s services are deliberately focused, targeted and catalytic, prioritizing areas where the IFRC Secretariat adds the greatest value in terms of coordination, accountability, and sustainability; the incumbent advances the delegation’s key shifts that underpin its operating model, ensuring that international support results in stronger, more sustainable and locally led humanitarian action The incumbent reports to the Head of Delegation, with technical supervision provided by the Deputy Regional Director. The incumbent serves as Head of Office for the Democratic Republic of the Congo for internal management and operational matters, while external representation and cluster-wide leadership remain exercised within the single Head of Delegation and Deputy Head of Delegation structure covering the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, the Republic of the Congo and Rwanda. Job Purpose Under the supervision of the Head of Delegation, the Deputy Head of Delegation supports the strategic leadership, overall management and effective performance of the Country Cluster Delegation, ensuring continuity of leadership and deputizing for the Head of Delegation as delegated. The role contributes to the delegation’s strategic and operational direction, institutional risk oversight, external representation, and cross-functional coordination, while providing specific leadership for National Society Development, Membership Coordination, Accountability and organisational agility. The post holder partners with the leadership of National Societies in strengthening governance, leadership, sustainability, integrity, and organisational effectiveness while promoting ownership of, and mutual accountability for, jointly agreed commitments and results; promotes coherent engagement of IFRC members behind National Society priorities; and advances localisation, accountability, transparency, and adaptive ways of working in line with IFRC Secretariat Renewal, the IFRC Network Way of Working and IFRC’s constitutional mandates. Through these responsibilities, the role provides strategic leadership to IFRC efforts to strengthen National Societies as accountable, sustainable, locally led, and effective actors and contributes to the effective delivery of the Country Cluster Delegation’s overall strategic objectives. Job Duties And Responsibilities National Society Development Lead IFRC Secretariat support and coordinate country-level IFRC Network cooperation in support of National Society Development (NSD) priorities. Advise and partner with National Society leaders to strengthen governance, leadership, organisational culture, integrity, sustainability and institutional effectiveness. Enable National Society-led organisational transformation by supporting leaders to diagnose systemic challenges, define strategic choices, build consensus and translate agreed decisions into measurable and sustained institutional change. Coordinate the use of relevant assessments, evidence and investment frameworks to inform coherent NSD strategies, plans, resource mobilisation and monitoring. Ensure that emergency operations, programmes and partnerships contribute to enduring National Society capacity, systems and sustainability. IFRC Membership Coordination Lead implementation of the IFRC Network Way of Working and promote coherent engagement of the IFRC Secretariat and supporting member National Societies behind host National Society priorities. Provide cluster-level leadership, quality assurance and strategic support for membership coordination, while enabling each National Society to lead country-level coordination and cooperation arrangements in its own context. Partner with National Society leaders to convene, coordinate and align IFRC Network support around nationally defined priorities and strategic objectives. Promote unified planning, complementary implementation, joint monitoring, coordinated resource mobilisation and transparent support arrangements. Establish and facilitate mechanisms through which IFRC Network components review progress against jointly agreed commitments, address underperformance, agree corrective measures and practise mutual accountability National Society Accountability, Integrity and Institutional Risk Advise, challenge and enable National Society leaders to foster accountability, openness, transparency, ethical leadership, responsible risk-taking and responsible stewardship. Advise and support National Society leaders to strengthen integrity systems, safeguarding measures, accountability frameworks, community feedback and complaints mechanisms, and risk management practices. Partner with National Society leaders to identify and address institutional performance gaps and risks that may affect effectiveness, credibility or sustainability. Support the HoD in the oversight of delegation-wide strategic and institutional risks, ensuring appropriate analysis, mitigation, escalation and follow-up in coordination with relevant risk owners and technical functions. Promote accountability to communities, including transparency, safeguarding, responsiveness to feedback and evidence of results. Job Duties And Responsibilities (continued) IFRC Secretariat Renewal, Agility and Organisational Performance Coordinate and monitor implementation of the delegation’s agreed Renewal commitments, facilitate cross-functional follow-up, and advise the management team on progress, constraints and corrective action. Identify duplication, decision bottlenecks and unnecessary bureaucracy, and support simpler, faster and more effective ways of working while maintaining appropriate accountability and risk controls. Promote clear decision rights, delegated authority, cross-functional collaboration, adaptive management and evidence-based prioritisation. Anticipate emerging issues and escalate significant governance, integrity, accountability or risk concerns through appropriate IFRC mechanisms. Promote a culture of continuous improvement, learning and responsible innovation, and monitor agreed organisational performance improvements. Strategic Leadership Ensure continuity of delegation leadership by deputising for the Head of Delegation and exercising delegated strategic, operational, representational and management responsibilities. Serve as principal adviser to the Head of Delegation, contributing to the strategic and operational direction of the Country Cluster Delegation through analysis, problem-solving, prioritisation, decision support and oversight of implementation. Support the overall management and performance of the Country Cluster Delegation, including strategic planning, resource allocation, operational continuity, cross-functional coordination and resolution of significant management or delivery issues. Position the IFRC Secretariat as a trusted adviser, convener and enabler to National Society leadership, supporting ownership, institutional development, accountability and sustainable progress. Represent the IFRC and, when delegated, the Head of Delegation in engagement with National Society leadership, Movement partners, government counterparts, donors, humanitarian actors and other stakeholders. Team and Portfolio Management Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team, setting clear objectives, priorities, accountabilities and performance expectations. Foster a high-performing, inclusive and collaborative culture, ensuring effective staff performance management, development, wellbeing and succession planning. Oversee portfolio planning, budgeting, resource allocation, monitoring and reporting in accordance with IFRC policies, delegated authorities and agreed priorities. Promote effective matrix management and collaboration across country, regional and global functions, reference centres, National Societies and IFRC Network partners. Champion a safe, respectful and inclusive work environment, actively preventing and addressing harassment, discrimination, abuse of authority, sexual exploitation and abuse, and other forms of misconduct. Serve as a trusted and accessible point of contact for concerns related to inappropriate conduct, ensuringconcerns are handled promptly, confidentially and in a victim-centred manner in accordance with IFRC policies. The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is the region’s premier political and economic policy organisation and serves as the Secretariat of the Pacific Islands Forum. Guided by the Agreement Establishing the Pacific Islands Forum (2005) and the decisions of Forum Leaders, PIFS supports Forum Members to strengthen regional cooperation and integration and advance shared priorities for economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. PIFS leads regional coordination for the implementation of the 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent. The Strategy calls for a long-term regional commitment to act as one “Blue Continent” as the means to achieve development aspirations. Its implementation requires a credible and sustainable evidence base that connects regional priorities, collective actions and initiatives to clear data, learning and accountability, that enables Leaders, officials and partners to understand progress, identify gaps and make informed decisions. The regional data ecosystem is rich but fragmented. Data on Pacific progress exists across National Statistical Offices and various Ministries, UN agencies, SPC that provides Secretariat for Pacific Regional Data Governance Architecture and manages the Pacific Data Hub, and other CROP organisations and development partners, but it is not consistently connected to 2050 Strategy reporting, nor systematically used to inform partnerships, policy analysis or advocacy across the regional architecture. At the same time, PIFS is approaching major milestones that will require a stronger, more integrated evidence base than the current systems, including the 2027 Outcome Report, the 2028 Deep Dive thematic analysis, and the Phase 1 review of the 2050 Strategy. To address this, this role will provide support to strengthen 2050 data systems, triangulate regional evidence sources, connect the 2050 data to the wider regional data ecosystem and support analysis of data on regional priorities. The assignment will be delivered in close collaboration with the 2050 MEL Adviser, the Adviser Data Analytics and Insights, and key regional partners including the Pacific Community (SPC), the Pacific Data Hub, UNICEF Pacific, National Statistical Offices, CROP agencies, United Nations agencies and other development partners. The consultancy is supported under the PIFS–UNICEF Pacific Memorandum of Understanding. review_candidates.description: Dich begeistern Creatives, die nicht nur gut aussehen, sondern skalieren? Du willst von grafischer Seite unmittelbar daran mitwirken, dass ein Onlineshop wächst – und in den Zahlen sehen, was dein Hook, dein Static, dein Banner bewegt? Dann bist du bei NEOLYMP richtig. Wir skalieren unseren Shop, und ein großer Teil davon entscheidet sich im Creative. Genau da sitzt du: als Creative Designer:in, der oder die aus Design- und Grafiksicht maßgeblich an unserer Performance mitwirkt. Wer wir sind NEOLYMP ist eine Berliner Fitnessmarke, gegründet 2018. Wir entwickeln innovatives Fitnessequipment und ganzheitliche Trainingskonzepte für zu Hause – vom durchdachten Home-Gym-Equipment bis hin zu Online-Kursen, die Training, Motivation und Alltag zusammenbringen. Unsere Produkte verkaufen wir über Amazon und unseren eigenen Onlineshop. Content ist bei uns der Motor: Wir bauen unsere Inhouse-Creative-Produktion konsequent aus – mit echten Shootings, einem Creator-Netzwerk und KI-gestützten Workflows. Unser Grafikteam wächst, und wir suchen jemanden, der das gesamte visuelle Spektrum abdeckt. Warum diese Rolle Du bist Teil der Performance: Deine Creatives laufen im Paid-Marketing und entscheiden mit, wie profitabel wir skalieren. Du siehst in den Zahlen, welcher Hook funktioniert, welches Static klickt – und drehst mit jeder Iteration an einem Hebel, der direkt auf Umsatz wirkt. Alles aus einer Hand: Video-Creatives, Statics, Social-Content, Shop-Banner, Produktbilder – du bist die zentrale Anlaufstelle für alles Visuelle und siehst deine Arbeit überall: in Ads, im Feed, im Shop. Bestes Rohmaterial: Du arbeitest mit Content aus echten Shootings und von echten Creatorn – kein Stockmaterial, sondern Persönlichkeiten und Produkte, die du in Szene setzt. Grafikteam statt Einzelkämpfer: Du arbeitest mit Kolleg:innen, die Grafik, Content und Creator verantworten, und eng mit Marketing und Performance zusammen. KI als Werkzeug, nicht als Ersatz: Du nutzt KI-Tools, um schneller zu Varianten und Ideen zu kommen – und entscheidest als Designer:in, was davon gut ist. Aufgaben Performance Creatives Du schneidest Video-Creatives für Meta, TikTok und weitere Paid-Kanäle – vom Rohmaterial aus Shootings und Creator-Content bis zum fertigen Ad, inklusive Hook-Varianten, Untertiteln und Sound. Du gestaltest Static Ads, die in Sekunden verstanden werden, und entwickelst sie auf Basis der Performance-Daten iterativ weiter. Du setzt Briefings aus dem Performance-Team um und bringst eigene Ideen für Formate, Hooks und Varianten ein. Social Media & Organic Content Du produzierst Grafiken, Reels-Schnitte, Story-Formate und Carousels für unsere organischen Kanäle – konsistent im Look, angepasst an jede Plattform. Du entwickelst Templates, die dem Content-Team schnelle, markenkonforme Veröffentlichungen ermöglichen. Shop, Amazon & Brand Du bist Ansprechpartner:in für alle Bannerbilder, Kampagnen-Visuals und Shopbilder – von Landingpage-Headern. Du hältst unser visuelles Erscheinungsbild über alle Kanäle konsistent und entwickelst es gemeinsam mit dem Team weiter. Produktion & Workflow Du integrierst KI-Tools in deinen Workflow – für Ideation, Bildvarianten, Freisteller, Übersetzungen oder Schnitt-Unterstützung – und teilst mit dem Team, was funktioniert. Qualifikation Das brauchst du auf jeden Fall Schnitterfahrung: Du beherrschst Videoschnitt sicher – Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve oder vergleichbar – und lieferst aus Rohmaterial eigenständig fertige, plattformgerechte Video-Creatives inklusive Schnittrhythmus, Text-Overlays, Untertiteln und Sound. Bildbearbeitung & Grafik: Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma oder vergleichbare Tools sind dein Handwerkszeug. Freisteller, Retusche, Composings, Layouts und saubere Exportformate für Web, Social und Amazon gehen dir leicht von der Hand. Ein Portfolio, das beides zeigt – Video und Static. Das ist uns außerdem wichtig Mehrjährige Erfahrung als Grafik-, Motion- oder Creative Designer:in, idealerweise im E-Commerce, D2C oder in einer Performance-Agentur. Ein Verständnis dafür, was Performance Creatives von schönen Grafiken unterscheidet: Hook, Klarheit, Tempo, Lesbarkeit auf dem Handy. Gespür für Social-Plattformen: Du weißt, wie Content auf TikTok, Instagram und Pinterest aussehen muss, um nicht weggewischt zu werden. Strukturierte Arbeitsweise: Du jonglierst mehrere Aufträge parallel, hältst Deadlines und behältst den Überblick über Formate, Versionen und Assets. Das zählt für uns am meisten Lust darauf, wirklich das ganze visuelle Spektrum zu bespielen, Neugier auf neue Tools und die Motivation, mit der Rolle und dem Team zu wachsen. Das Handwerk setzen wir voraus – für alles darüber hinaus ist uns Drive wichtiger als das perfekte Profil. Nice to have Erfahrung mit KI-Tools in der Bild- oder Videoproduktion (z. B. Midjourney, Runway, Firefly, ElevenLabs). Fotografie- oder Kamera-Erfahrung für Shootings. Kenntnisse in Shopify (Bildformate, Theme-Assets) oder Amazon-Bildrichtlinien. Erfahrung im Fitness- oder Sport-Umfeld. Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt unter „außerdem wichtig“? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Uns interessiert dein Portfolio und wie du denkst – nicht, ob du jede Zeile abhaken kannst. Benefits DAS BIETEN WIR DIR Flexibles Arbeiten: Du arbeitest überwiegend remote und profitierst von flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, die dir eine eigenverantwortliche Gestaltung deines Arbeitsalltags ermöglichen. Zu Shootings triffst du das Team vor Ort – der Rest läuft von dort, wo du am besten arbeitest. Attraktive Zusatzleistungen: Neben moderner Hardware und den Tools, die du brauchst, erhältst du eine Spenditcard mit monatlich 50 € steuerfreiem Sachbezug sowie ein persönliches Educational Budget für deine fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung. Verantwortung & Gestaltungsspielraum: Du prägst das visuelle Erscheinungsbild einer wachsenden Marke und gestaltest den Aufbau unserer Inhouse-Creative-Produktion aktiv mit – inklusive KI-basierter Workflows. Dynamisches Startup-Umfeld: Freue dich auf kurze Entscheidungswege, regelmäßige Team-Events und ein modernes Arbeitsumfeld in einer schnell wachsenden E-Commerce-Marke. Klingt nach dir? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung – und darauf, dich kennenzulernen. Kontakt: Josephine Steuer Wir glauben, dass Vielfalt uns stärker macht. Deshalb heißen wir alle Bewerbenden willkommen, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion, Alter, sexueller Identität oder Behinderung. Bei uns gibt es keinen Dresscode und wir duzen uns einfach. Der Einfachheit halber verwenden wir im Text eine Sprachform, schließen damit aber ausdrücklich alle Menschen ein.

review_candidates.title: Community Outreach Program Manager
review_candidates.description: Join Community Community Health Network was created by our neighbors, for our neighbors. Over 60 years later, “community” is still the heart of our organization. It means providing our neighbors with the best care possible, backed by state-of-the-art technology. It means getting involved in the communities we serve through volunteer opportunities and benefits initiatives. It means ensuring our dedicated caregivers can learn and grow to stay at the top of their fields and to better serve our patients. And above all, it means exceptional care, simply delivered — and we couldn’t do it without you. Make a Difference The Community Outreach Program Manager advances Community Health Network's commitment to improving community health through meaningful partnerships, strategic outreach, sponsorship support, community benefit initiatives, and volunteer engagement. This role serves as a connector between the Network and the communities it serves by developing collaborative relationships, coordinating impactful outreach initiatives, and ensuring community engagement efforts align with organizational priorities and identified community needs. Working across the Network, this leader collaborates with internal stakeholders, community organizations, and caregiver volunteers to execute outreach strategies that support Community Health Network's mission of enhancing the health and well-being of Central Indiana residents. Exceptional Skills And Qualifications Applicants for this position should be able to build collaborative community relationships, manage multiple cross-functional initiatives, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, and use data to evaluate community impact and guide outreach strategies. Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Healthcare Administration, Communications, Nonprofit Management, Business, Social Work, or a related field required. Five or more years of experience in community outreach, community engagement, nonprofit partnerships, healthcare, public health, or a related field required. Three or more years of experience planning and executing community events and volunteer programs required. Demonstrated experience managing community partnerships and cross-functional initiatives preferred. Experience with Community Benefit reporting or Community Health Needs Assessment preferred. Collaborates with the Network Sponsorship Committee and internal and external partners to fulfill sponsorship commitments and maximize the visibility, effectiveness, and community impact of sponsored programs, events, and initiatives. Supports the planning and execution of the Network's triennial Community Health Needs Assessment and helps develop initiatives that address identified priority health needs. Oversees the collection, tracking, documentation, and reporting of community engagement activities to support Community Benefit requirements and organizational and regulatory standards. Analyzes community engagement data and outcomes to evaluate impact, identify trends, and inform future outreach strategies and programming. review_candidates.description: What We Do The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) works worldwide to provide humanitarian protection and assistance to people affected by conflict and armed violence. We take action in response to emergencies and at the same time promote respect for international humanitarian law. We are an independent and neutral organization, and our mandate stems essentially from the Geneva Conventions of 1949. We work closely with National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and with their International Federation in order to ensure a concerted, rational and rapid humanitarian response to the needs of the victims of armed conflict or any other situation of internal violence. We direct and coordinate the international activities conducted in these situations. Purpose Language is at the heart of humanitarian action; it enables dialogue, builds trust, and ensures that people affected by conflict can express themselves and be heard. The ICRC Interpreter plays a critical role in enabling this by facilitating accurate and meaningful communication among ICRC delegates, affected populations, authorities, and other stakeholders. Through interpretation in sensitive and complex contexts, including protection activities, visits to detainees, family reunification processes, and dialogue with parties to conflict, the Interpreter ensures that every conversation can take place with clarity, respect, and confidentiality. This is a unique, people-centered role that goes beyond translating words. It requires judgment, cultural awareness, and a deep understanding of the humanitarian principles guiding the ICRC’s work, helping build bridges of understanding where communication can make a real difference. Accountabilities & Functional Responsibilities Oral interpretation: from Arabic to English and vice versa during confidential interviews with people deprived of liberty, ICRC institutional dissemination, ICRC dialogue with authorities, activities to establish the family links which includes delivering Red Cross messages, family tracing and visits to families of detainees. Written translation: translation of Arabic language (newspaper articles, correspondence, etc.) into written English. Analysis and reporting as required: analysis of conditions of detention, security and other matters relating to the ICRC's mandate. Can be asked to provide support on other protection activities as needed. Relationships Externally, interacts with the authorities, representatives of other organizations and beneficiaries, both within and outside places of detention. May be called upon to develop a network of contacts related to operational needs. Internally, interacts with staff in other departments. Required Profile And Skills Excellent command of English (C1) required Excellent command of Arabic (C1) required Proficiency in other ICRC operational languages (English, French, Spanish, Russian, Arabic, Portuguese) is a strong asset. 2 years of professional experience. Previous interpreter or translator experience is an advantage. Strongly motivated by humanitarian work. Able to work under pressure in a potentially dangerous environment. Open-minded and adaptable. University education/degree in interpretation or translation is an advantage. Our operational & field constraints In line with the principle of neutrality, the ICRC does not assign personnel to a country of which they are nationals. Candidates must be in good health and will have to do a medical check-up prior to departure in the field. Candidates must possess a driving licence (for manual transmission vehicles). Candidates must be prepared to accept unaccompanied postings (i.e. no spouse, partner, children or dependents) for the first two missions (minimum 12 months each) or total of 24 months. What We Offer Rewarding work in a humanitarian and multicultural environment A two-week orientation course and other opportunities for further in-house training Attractive social benefits Join an ICRC talent pool and be considered for future assignments elsewhere The ICRC values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates! Our values At the ICRC, we value impact, collaboration, respect, and compassion. We seek candidates who demonstrate behaviors based on these shared values. For more information on the ICRC values, please visit this page. Additional Information Type of role: Mobile Working rate: 100% Starting date: Continuous, global deployment roster. Location: Near & Middle East Region, various contexts Hardship : Variable Job level: B2 Length of assignment: 12 months, extendable Contract type: Maximum-term contract
